A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAD-TD and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original DMC experiments, including learning curves, value-estimation measurements, and model-data, resetting, and robustness ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds SynthER comparisons, further ablations, and results on nine MetaWorld tasks.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same TD3-based architecture, latent world model, training losses, default 5% generated critic data, and optional MPC. The new TD-MPC2 ablation evaluates the existing design rather than introducing a method revision.

E1.justification: DMC-only evaluation expands to nine MetaWorld manipulation tasks, including assembly, lever-pull, and pick-place-wall (v2 Appendix E.8, Figure 22). The broader DMC coverage already present in v1 Appendix E.5 is retained as v2 Appendix E.7.

E2.justification: v1 compares against BRO and TD-MPC2 but explicitly lacks a SynthER comparison. v2 evaluates this directly relevant data-generation competitor on the hard DMC suite (E.4, Figure 15). It also directly compares the no-generated-data MAD-TD control with TD-MPC2 in E.5.

E3.justification: Existing DMC budgets, action-repeat comparisons, and default update ratios remain unchanged. Added experimental settings extend the generated-data sweep from 0%, 5%, and 50% to include 25%, 75%, 95%, and 100%, and introduce a UTD-1, zero-generated-data comparison with TD-MPC2.

E4.justification: The expanded mixing-ratio analysis tests failure under excessive model-generated data (E.3). A new comparison across 18 DMC tasks examines whether simplifying the TD-MPC2 base architecture explains performance differences (E.5). Existing resetting, random-action, model-size, MPC, and adversarial analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten seeds for main result curves and 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals in Section 5. v2 introduces no changed run-count policy, uncertainty-estimation procedure, or explicit significance-testing method.

E6.justification: v2 adds results showing degradation at high generated-data fractions, poor SynthER performance on most hard DMC tasks, broadly similar performance in the base-model control, and mixed MetaWorld performance with sparse-reward difficulties. These extend the evidence substantially; the retained main-result curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: The linear-feature stability argument, Proposition 1, and Appendix C derivations retain their mathematical substance. Equation numbering and typesetting corrections do not introduce new assumptions, results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's two stated contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about action misgeneralization and stabilizing high-UTD learning with small amounts of generated data. The conclusion adds a pointer to existing limitations without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially extends the failure analysis beyond v1's general exploration caveats. It attributes high model-data degradation to model exploitation (E.3), explains dense-versus-sparse-reward behavior on MetaWorld, and proposes TD3 policy saturation as an exploration failure mechanism (E.8). Appendix A itself remains unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds a code-repository link, and Appendix B now states that the original SynthER implementation was rerun. The architecture and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; these additions primarily improve access and experiment provenance.

R1.justification: v2 adds an offline-RL discussion with references to Lange, Fujimoto, Jin, and Yu, plus the MetaWorld benchmark citation. SynthER is more explicitly positioned as testing a competing explanation for high-UTD failures. The broader related-work framework remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are retained. Local prose and caption edits, corrected cross-references, numbered equations, updated affiliations and acknowledgments, and targeted new appendix subsections refine the document without extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 expands Figure 13 and adds an aggregate mixing-ratio display and multi-panel SynthER, base-model-control, and MetaWorld figures. Existing figures and tables are substantially reflowed and resized; Figures 9–10 move before the references, and appendix plots are regrouped.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important gaps by evaluating SynthER, adding a control for the modified TD-MPC2 architecture, and testing beyond DMC. The expanded mixing-ratio study and MetaWorld failures strengthen empirical support while clarifying applicability limits. Although the new experimental protocols remain briefly documented, these additions substantially improve the paper's evidential foundation.
